source: Existing human-curated Movie Mood catalogue; non-evaluation examples used only by the Phase 5B replay.

positiveExamples.rationale: A brisk comic caper can still feel controlled and restorative; fast pace does not rule out relaxing.
Ensemble comedy and playful momentum can support a shared friends viewing fit.
Romantic warmth and manageable viewing cost can support date-night without requiring a literal label.
Accessible whimsical framing can support easy-watch while remaining specific rather than generic.
Quiet presentation can still carry sustained emotional cost; do not equate slow or restrained with light.
Observational pacing is independent from immersive attention demand and heavy emotional weight.

boundaryAndCounterexamples.contrast: fast is not incompatible with relaxing
boundaryAndCounterexamples.reviewNote: Treat brisk controlled comedy as a possible supported inference when multiple factual cues support it.

boundaryAndCounterexamples.contrast: relaxing does not automatically mean easy-watch
boundaryAndCounterexamples.reviewNote: A film may support a social friends fit without qualifying for easy-watch; assess each situation independently.

boundaryAndCounterexamples.contrast: date-night is not limited to explicit romance labels
boundaryAndCounterexamples.reviewNote: Use grounded relational and practical viewing cues rather than requiring literal taxonomy wording.

boundaryAndCounterexamples.contrast: slow and restrained can still be heavy
boundaryAndCounterexamples.reviewNote: Protect against emotional-weight undershoot when factual cues indicate sustained emotional consequence.

boundaryAndCounterexamples.contrast: exciting is not the sole proof of fast pace
boundaryAndCounterexamples.reviewNote: Use movement and narrative-pressure cues for pace; do not infer fast only from an excitement label.
